source_use_records.source_and_role: Krystyna Mruczek-Nasieniewska and Mateusz Klonowski, *Decomposition of Płonka sums into direct systems*, [arXiv:2402.14681v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14681v3), 26 March 2024, Theorem 26
source_use_records.qualification: The retained primary preprint statement was checked. Its hypothesis is a nontrivial system of algebras isolated with respect to the given algebra; its conclusion recovers a direct system and its Płonka sum. source_use_records.source_and_role: Juan Climent Vidal and Enric Cosme Llópez, *Płonka adjunction*, [published DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/jigpal/jzae064); checked [arXiv:2305.03581v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03581v2), 11 May 2023, Propositions 7.15 and 7.39
source_use_records.qualification: In this exact preprint version, Proposition 7.15 proves that the inductive-system functor has the Płonka construction as left adjoint; 7.39 gives essential surjectivity and states that counit components are isomorphisms. The signature excludes nullary operations. The 2025 journal issue was authenticated, but the numbered propositions here are verified in v2, not silently transferred to a different published layout.

source_use_records.use_locator: C10A lines 202–210: finite support retract comparison
source_use_records.source_and_role: Friedrich Wehrung, *Distributive semilattices as retracts of ultraboolean ones; functorial inverses without adjunction*, [arXiv:math/0409263v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409263v2), 30 August 2005, Theorem 9.5
source_use_records.qualification: Checked exact theorem and subsequent properties: finite distributive join-semilattices with zero admit functorial finite Boolean retractions on the category with embeddings. The maps retain the stated zero/unit properties; the retraction satisfies \(\mu_A\epsilon_A=\mathrm{id}_A\). This supplies a support-side comparison, not the additional \(R\)-module increment classification.

source_use_records.source_and_role: Serge Bouc and Jacques Thévenaz, *The representation theory of finite sets and correspondences*, [HAL hal-01214177v2](https://hal.science/hal-01214177v2), Theorem 11.11
source_use_records.qualification: The complete theorem statement and proof were read in the retained primary text: for a finite lattice \(T\), its associated correspondence functor \(F_T\) is projective exactly when \(T\) is distributive. The functor category is not identified with \(G(R)\)-semimodules. Credit it as the stated comparison, not as the source of the project's \(R\)-module normal form.

source_use_records.source_and_role: Yefim Katsov, Tran Giang Nam and Jens Zumbrägel, *On congruence-semisimple semirings and the \(K_0\)-group characterization of ultramatricial algebras over semifields*, Fact 4.6
source_use_records.qualification: The statement was checked in [arXiv:1711.05163v1](https://arxiv.org/html/1711.05163v1): Boolean-semimodule projectivity is equivalent to being a distributive lattice with finite principal lower ideals. **Its displayed citation is Horn–Kimura, Theorem 5.3.** The human chain must include those earlier authors, not stop at this modern restatement.

source_use_records.source_and_role: Alfred Horn and Naoki Kimura, *The category of semilattices*, *Algebra Universalis* 1 (1971), 26–38, [DOI `10.1007/BF02944952`](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02944952)
source_use_records.qualification: Publisher metadata authenticated. Theorem 5.3's original full text was not available in this pass; its exact role is established by the explicit primary-source citation in Katsov–Nam–Zumbrägel. Wehrung's proof also cites Horn–Kimura Theorem 2.10 for embeddings into injective semilattices. Do not claim an independent reread of that original theorem.
